- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 3–5 days.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or neutral, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to align with mean-reversion bias.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overshoots in subsequent days; apply a “cool-down” correction: reduce forecast by 2–5% for 2–4 days post-spike.
- Model underperforms in 30-day horizon when sentiment is volatile (alternating 0.33/1.00); use sentiment-weighted moving average to smooth forecast.
- If last 3–5 days show downward trend + negative sentiment, model often fails to recognize mean reversion; add 1–2% upward bias to counteract underestimation.
- When sentiment is high but price is flat or slightly declining, model tends to overreact; cap forecast at 1–2% above recent 7-day average to avoid overcorrection.
